messages:
Maya: Quick readout from the L4/T4/A10G bench across us-east1 / europe-west1 for embeddings and a small-chat workload (short convo, ~50 tokens). Wanted to share numbers and get sizing recs.

Maya: Run details: model=redwood-small-chat-v1 (8k context), embed-model=redwood-embed-1536, payloads: embeddings(batch=64), chat(batch=8, 50 tokens gen). Quant modes: fp16, q4_0, int8 (where supported). Kernels: cuBLASLt, CUTLASS, flash-attn.

Maya: Raw summary (p50/p95 lat in ms, throughput in req/s, cost/h assumed):
```
EMBEDDINGS (batch=64)
A10G  fp16  p50=3ms  p95=9ms   thr=1500 req/s   cost/h=$1.60   cost/1M embeds=$0.30
L4    q4_0  p50=4ms  p95=12ms  thr=1200 req/s   cost/h=$0.80   cost/1M embeds=$0.19
T4    q4_0  p50=6ms  p95=18ms  thr=900  req/s   cost/h=$0.30   cost/1M embeds=$0.09

SMALL-CHAT (~50 tok/resp, batch=8)
A10G  fp16  p50=40ms  p95=95ms  tok/sec=3500   cost/h=$1.60   cost/1M tok=$0.13
L4    q4_0  p50=70ms  p95=140ms tok/sec=2200   cost/h=$0.80   cost/1M tok=$0.10
T4    q4_0  p50=110ms p95=230ms tok/sec=1500   cost/h=$0.30   cost/1M tok=$0.06
```
Notes: numbers averaged over 2h runs, 95% CI ~±6%.

Tony: Nice. A few quick takeaways: 1) A10G wins latency & raw throughput for FP16 chat (best p95), but cost/hr is high so cost/1M depends on utilization. 2) T4 is cheapest-per-unit for steady high-throughput embedding pipelines if you can tolerate higher p95. 3) L4 sits in the middle and is a good sweet spot for mixed workloads where latency matters but budget is constrained.

Tony: Kernel/quant notes: on A10G we pinned to cuBLASLt + CUTLASS for matmul and enabled flash-attn for short sequences; gave ~12-18% token/sec boost vs generic cuBLAS. On L4 q4_0 with Triton kernels improved batch-8 chat throughput (KV cache memory friendly). T4 had more kernel variance across regions (some hosts fell back to cuBLAS which inflated p95).

Liam: Region differences observed: us-east1 consistently ~5-12% lower p95 vs europe-west1 for chat (same instance types) — likely due to host kernel build and NIC config. Also note: our dedicated L4 fleet in europe-west1 uses a slightly older driver (470.x) which caused fallback to slower kernels for some q4 paths; upgrading to 525.x removes the regression.

Sarah: Any stability/failure modes? Did you see OOMs or degrads when forcing int8/q8?

Maya: Int8 was unstable on T4 for the chat model — we saw 0.3% correctness regressions (diff vs fp16 on a 1k eval set) and occasional CUDA OOM on long contexts. q4_0 was stable across L4/A10G for both workloads. We ran eval suites (1000 prompts) to measure quality drift; int8 had measurable hallucination increase on multi-turn prompts, so we flagged it as "experimental".

Tony: For capacity sizing here's a rough rule-of-thumb from these numbers:
```
Service: embeddings (1M req/day) -> config examples:
- T4 (q4): 1 GPU -> ~3.24M req/hr peak -> comfortably handles daily 1M if traffic is bursty but watch latency.
- L4 (q4): 1 GPU -> ~4.32M req/hr -> better latency, medium cost.
- A10G (fp16): 1 GPU -> ~5.4M req/hr -> lowest latency but >2x cost vs T4.
Service: small-chat (10M tok/day) -> approximate GPUs needed (steady)
- A10G: 10M tok/day ~ 116 tok/sec -> 1 A10G can do 3500 tok/s -> 1 GPU plenty; but for p95 SLAs you might want 2 for headroom and fallback.
- L4: 1 GPU = 2200 tok/s -> still plenty; choose 1-2.
- T4: 1 GPU = 1500 tok/s -> also plenty but p95 higher; for low-latency product use A10G or L4.
```
Numbers assume no sharing with heavy batching workloads.

Liam: Also account for regional capacity constraints — europe-west1 L4 stock is limited, so autoscaling burst to A10G in us-central is a reasonable fallback policy. We tested smart routing: prefer local L4 for cost, fallback to A10G cross-region if latency SLO is violated. That kept p95 <200ms in our simulated PLG traffic.

Maya: Actions: 1) I'll add these bench tables to the internal perf playbook. 2) Mark int8 as "experimental" for chat models (don't enable by default). 3) Add driver/kernel version to onboarding checklist (L4 needs >=525.x).

bench-bot: Auto-summary generated: 1752345678 | embeds: T4 cheapest per-embed, L4 balanced, A10G fastest. chat: A10G best latency, L4 good middle ground, T4 cheapest but higher p95. Region: eu vs us ~10% p95 delta; driver versions affect kernel choices.

Sarah: Can you also paste the exact bench commands/flags used (so infra can re-run for other regions)?

Maya: Pasted simplified runner flags:
```
./bench-runner --model redwood-small-chat-v1 --embed-model redwood-embed-1536 \
  --gpu A10G --batch_chat 8 --batch_embed 64 --quant fp16 --kernels cuBLASLt,flash-attn
./bench-runner --gpu L4 --quant q4_0 --kernels triton,cutlass
./bench-runner --gpu T4 --quant q4_0 --kernels cutlass
```
I'll drop the full scripts in #eng-infra and link them from the perf playbook.

Tony: Cool. Can you tag me when updated? I'll try a longer run with dynamic batching and measure cost savings with caching. :thumbsup:

Maya: Will do — ping me if you want the raw CSVs (I kept p50/p95/p99 + token distributions).
